snp5.9:3.4: The word accuta carries both senses at once: “unfallen” and “undying.”
snp5.9:4.3: Following the Burmese, Sri Lankan, and PTS editions’ sadā (“always”). The Thai edition instead reads satā (“mindful”), but that would just repeat satā from the line before it, a repetition Pali poetry generally avoids except for deliberate emphasis.
